ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals (SDN) and Non-SDN lists, United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions Lists, Canadian Autonomous Sanctions Lists under the Special Economic Measures Act (including Russia, Venezuela, Iran, Syria), and domestic PEP lists as defined by FINTRAC (domestic and foreign PEPs, politically exposed persons, heads of state, senior officials, and family members). Enhanced risk-based due diligence is prescribed for high-risk jurisdictions (FATF black/grey list), and ongoing transaction monitoring is required under PCMLTFA. For ISIC 4649 pharmaceutical API bulk wholesale, additional screening against the Canadian Food and Drugs Act prohibited parties and customs/health enforcement databases is recommended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (via ISED) - https://www.ic.gc.ca/ci/ic/ns/cc-rc.nsf/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), a federal corporate name may be in English, French, or both; for names in a non-official language, a transliteration (phonetic equivalent in English or French) or translation must be furnished. The name must include a legal element: Limited, Ltd., Incorporated, Inc., Corporation, Corp., or the French equivalents Société par actions, S.A., or Limitée. The name must not be confusingly similar to existing corporate names, trademarks, or prior NUANS reports. Distinctiveness and descriptiveness rules under Section 12 of the CBCA and the Canadian Business Corporations Regulations (SOR/2001-512) apply.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Director of Corporations Canada, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration to the Director within 60 days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and non-confusion and submitting a revised NUANS search report if necessary. The Director's decision is subject to judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada. In practice, counsel commonly files an administrative appeal under section 213 of the CBCA or re-submits with a distinct suggested name. The pre-incorporation name reservation (NUANS report) remains valid for 90 days from issuance; a new NUANS report must be obtained if the reservation lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are generally not acceptable as a registered office for a CBCA corporation unless they correspond to a physical location in the province of registered office where process serving is actually possible and where corporate records can be produced. For ISIC 4649 pharmaceutical API wholesale distribution, Health Canada's Drug Licensing framework requires a physical establishment (or contract with a licensed importer/distributor) for good distribution practices (GDP). Therefore, a pure virtual office without physical commercial substance is unlikely to pass regulatory review; a licensed or contracted physical facility (or a third-party logistics provider with a Canadian location) is effectively mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% - Unannounced on-site inspections are likely due to: (i) the high-risk pharmaceutical license (Health Canada GDP license) requiring inspection at establishment; (ii) FINTRAC AML compliance on-site reviews; (iii) Canada Revenue Agency corporate tax verification visits. Frequency is elevated for entities handling active pharmaceutical ingredients.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended: s. 3 (incorporation by articles), s. 4 (capacity), s. 5 (name), s. 6 (articles), s. 7 (certificate of incorporation), s. 19 (registered office), s. 34 (share certificates), s. 102 (directors), s. 106 (restrictions on directors), s. 121 (officers), s. 124 (indemnification); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed under Section 6 of the Canada Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the CBCA. Shares may be issued for consideration in money, property, or past services; the consideration must be fully paid before a share certificate is issued. No escrow account requirement applies to a general federal corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for Common Shares set out in the incorporation subscription agreement be and is hereby accepted, and that such shares be allotted and issued upon full payment in accordance with section 25 of the CBCA. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [address], in the Province of [Province], and that the register of directors and records be maintained there. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED, that the President and Secretary are authorized to execute all post-incorporation filings, open corporate bank accounts, and effect any ancillary corporate actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via the NUANS name search system, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) pre-screen through a registered search house or the Corporations Canada online portal. Obtain a NUANS report dated within 90 days before filing. Verify the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing names and does not contravene the CBCA name prohibitions. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered company designation (e.g., '1234567 Canada Inc.').
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (English and/or French form)
NUANS search report (if using a named company)
Director information: full name, residential address, and citizenship or ordinary residence status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or not distinguishable, obtain a revised NUANS report and file amended articles with a substituted name, or elect a numbered company designation without additional name-search fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada – Office of the Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute Articles of Incorporation specifying the authorized share structure, any share restrictions, the number of directors, and the initial registered office address. Each incorporator must sign the articles. Obtain signed Consents to Act as Director from each initial director, and complete the Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors form. Ensure the registered office is a physical address in Canada and not a post-office box, and that the first board of directors consists of at least one director who is not disqualified under the CBCA.
required_dossiers: Consents to Act as Director for each initial director
Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors form
NUANS report (if using a named company)
Director identification and residential address records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a deficiency notice or rejects the filing, cure the deficiency by correcting the articles or consents and resubmitting within the stated response period. Legal counsel may assist in preparing a corrected filing if the rejection is based on technical non-compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation and accompanying forms through Corporations Canada's secure online portal or by mail to the Corporate Registry in Ottawa. Pay the applicable filing fee by credit card, debit, or certified cheque. After the statutory review, Corporations Canada will issue a Certificate of Incorporation under the corporate seal. Preserve the certificate and the filed articles as the corporation's founding constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or returned, comply with the written deficiency notice, correct the identified errors, and resubmit within 30 days. Additional fees may apply for excessive processing time unless the error was attributable to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Filing of Initial Return
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, complete and file the Initial Return with Corporations Canada within 181 days of incorporation. The Initial Return must state the registered office address, the names and residential addresses of directors, and a director's contact email address. The corporation may now commence business activities, subject to applicable industry licensing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is late, file immediately; failure to file may lead to administrative dissolution. A dissolved corporation may apply for revival under CBCA Part 2, subject to arrears and fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Passage of First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada records compliance; internal corporate records maintained at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors (or obtain unanimous written consent). Adopt the by-laws, confirm the share subscription and issuance, set the financial year end, select an auditor or waive the audit requirement, appoint officers, and adopt any banking resolutions. Ensure all share certificates are executed and delivered. This organizational step does not require a filing with Corporations Canada, but the resolutions must be recorded in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board meeting agenda and minutes or written resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share issuance is defective, pass a curative resolution ratifying the issuance and ensure consideration is fully paid and records are corrected. No registry filing is required unless the authorized share structure must be amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maintenance of Corporate Minute Book and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada compliance unit; records held at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and maintain a corporate minute book containing the articles, by-laws, organizational minutes, share register, director register, transfer ledger, and any registration certificates. Keep the registered office records updated to reflect any change of directors, officers, or registered office. Comply with annual return filing requirements under the CBCA before the anniversary date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are deficient or lost, reconstruct them from available filings and original documents, then pass curative resolutions. Correct any inconsistencies with Corporations Canada by filing the necessary updated forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada, Health Products and Food Branch, Office of Legislative and Regulatory Modernization; Office of Good Manufacturing Practices
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) under Division 1A of the Food and Drug Regulations, C.R.C., c. 870, C.01A.005

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) in coordination with provincial environmental ministries; for designated projects, the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt - not automatically subject to a full Impact Assessment Act report unless the facility involves new physical infrastructure exceeding federal designated thresholds; a site-specific environmental screening may be required under provincial law for hazardous waste storage or industrial wastewater discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA 1999) for toxic substances, VOC and particulate emission limits under provincial air quality regulations, the Fisheries Act for any effluent discharge, and the Hazardous Products Regulations for WHMIS-compliant storage. Wastewater from API handling must not contain active pharmaceutical ingredients above municipal sewer use by-law limits; hazardous pharmaceutical waste must be disposed through licensed waste carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire marshal or fire department, occupancy permit issued by the municipal building authority in conformance with the National Building Code of Canada and provincial building codes, structural load inspection for palletized and bulk pharmaceutical storage racks, and workplace clearance under the applicable provincial occupational health and safety statute. For facilities with regulated dangerous goods, the local authority must also issue a hazardous goods storage clearance and an emergency response plan must be approved.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal tax administration; official online portals: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO); International Tax Services Office for non-resident registrants.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporate API wholesaler obtains a CRA Business Number (BN) as its federal statutory tax identifier and registers for a GST/HST program account (RT) using CRA Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or the BRO portal. The entity must submit the RC1 before commencing taxable supplies in Canada. A non-resident corporation without a physical Canadian establishment may be required to provide a Canadian agent for service and evidence of Canadian business presence. The GST/HST account number is the VAT identifier for indirect tax purposes; the 9-digit BN plus a two-letter program account suffix serves for income tax, customs (RM account), and payroll where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Principal statutory elections relevant to a foreign corporation include: (i) the section 216 election for non-resident rental/timber income returns; (ii) the section 219 branch tax election for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada; (iii) certain private corporation elections (e.g., section 55 safe income adjustments); and (iv) hybrid mismatch coordinateion adjustments (sections 18.2, 18.3, 247.1) that do not create elective entity classification. No free-form passthrough election is available under federal law; classification follows the corporate legal charter.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; federal GST component and provincial component where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter for taxable supplies made by the person in Canada; once the threshold is exceeded in any single quarter, mandatory GST/HST registration applies effective on the day the threshold is exceeded. Non-resident API wholesalers supplying pharmaceutical ingredients from inventory located in Canada must monitor Canadian-source supplies against this threshold; small-supplier relief does not apply retroactively once exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government digital stamping, or pre-clearance e-invoice system for GST/HST. Registrants above the mandatory e-filing revenue threshold must transmit GST/HST returns and payments electronically through CRA-approved systems (GST/HST NETFILE, My Business Account, or financial institution electronic services). The CRA requires prescribed invoice data (seller name and GST/HST registration number, buyer identification, date, description, tax code and consideration) for input tax credit substantiation. Voluntary electronic invoicing is permitted, but no public infrastructure clearance or approval is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods made in Canada that are actually exported by the supplier or by the recipient, provided the goods leave Canada as part of the transaction and the supplier maintains contemporaneous export evidence. Supplies of services to a non-resident are zero-rated when the service is performed wholly or partly outside Canada and does not relate to Canadian real property; intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident is zero-rated if no right to use occurs in Canada. For pharmaceutical API bulk wholesale, the inventory must be shipped abroad under a genuine export transaction, with title passing to the foreign buyer and documentation demonstrating physical movement outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency export report and Canadian export documentation)
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail, or truck) evidencing the physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire / SWIFT MT103 / letter of credit payment documentation demonstrating receipt of foreign currency
Commercial Invoice issued by the Canadian API wholesaler
Non-resident buyer identity evidence and, where applicable, import licenses or regulatory approval for controlled pharmaceutical ingredients
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a GST/HST return within four years from the filing due date, an unlimited limitation period if misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. Failure to maintain the required export documentation invalidates the zero-rating and the GST/HST is clawed back, with penalties assessed under the Excise Tax Act including the false statement penalty under section 285.1 (minimum CAD 250 or, if greater, 50% of the evaded tax amount), gross negligence penalties, and criminal penalties for wilful evasion (fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment). Interest accrues from the date the unpaid tax was originally due.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); exchange-rate policy is set by the Governor-in-Council with the Minister of Finance; foreign exchange administration is conducted by the Bank of Canada under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act, with AML/CTF supervision by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating and fully convertible currency, accepted under IMF Article VIII status since 1952; there are no exchange controls limiting capital or current account convertibility. Both inbound and outbound funds may be freely transferred; profit remittance is subject only to withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25% dividend withholding, typically reduced to 5-15% under an applicable tax treaty) and does not involve central bank approval or any administrative convertibility hurdle. The practical legal friction is limited to FINTRAC AML reporting thresholds, CBSA cross-border currency declaration obligations for cash-equivalent instruments above CAD 10,000, and the Investment Canada Act national-security/public-interest review applicable to a pharmaceutical wholesale acquisition.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in Canadian bank foreign-currency accounts or offshore accounts without conversion obligation. However, proceeds for goods exports must be reported to Statistics Canada under the Canadian International Merchandise Trade statistics program and to the Canada Border Services Agency for customs; cross-border currency-reporting obligations apply to cash monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more transported across the border under section 12 of the PCMLTFA.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for core treasury purposes. Offshore fintech digital EMIs (e.g., UK-licensed electronic money institutions, EU EMI institutions, or global payment platforms such as Wise and Airwallex) are not authorized deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act; in Canada they may operate only as foreign money services businesses and must register with FINTRAC as an MSB and comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act if offering Canadian payment services. They cannot originate SWIFT documentary letters of credit, provide escrow-grade capital accounts, extend trade-finance facilities, or be used as the primary clearing bank for high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale treasury flows. Such platforms are acceptable only for ancillary collection and low-value disbursement use after FINTRAC registration and bank-grade KYC review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no Canadian federal statute that absolutely requires physical attendance by directors to open a corporate bank account. However, FINTRAC client-identification requirements and each Schedule I bank's own enhanced due diligence policy generally require a principal interview for a pharmaceutical API wholesale entity classified as High_Risk_Special_License. A physical in-branch appearance at an authorized Canadian branch is the customary norm; an alternative of a live video-conference interview with an authenticating officer may be accepted by certain Tier-1 banks only where combined with notarized corporate resolutions, certified passport copies, a beneficial-ownership register, and a documented signed risk questionnaire. Remote account opening is therefore possible but is the exception and is granted on a compliance-committee case-by-case basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where a non-resident 25%+ shareholder or a politically exposed person (PEP) is identified
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation; articles of amalgamation/continuation; complete register of directors and officers; full beneficial-ownership schedule with identification documents for each 25%+ holder; share transfer ledger; statutory declaration of ultimate ownership; source-of-wealth documents (bank statements, tax returns, business track record); and a FINTRAC-compliant written risk assessment narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical API product flagged as dual-use, controlled precursor, or regulated drug under Health Canada or international sanctions filtering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) held by the Canadian entity; schedule-level substance classification of each API with applicable DIN/NDS numbers; export/import permits under the Food and Drugs Act and the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (where applicable); customer-side controlled-substance licences; ISO/INN nomenclature and HTS tariff code listing; GMP or GGP certificates from each supplier; and a formal end-to-end supply-chain compliance descriptor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or beneficiary located in a high-risk jurisdiction or a sanctions-adjacent freight-forwarding/dealer layer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed international sale/purchase contracts with clear INCOTERMS; commercial LC or documentary collection terms (UCP600/URC522); invoices and tally sheets; bills of lading/airway bills; end-customer registry with ultimate-consignee declarations; completed sanctions and PEP screening results from a recognized screening vendor; and a corporate AML/ATF compliance manual with a geographic-risk matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment displacement or mixed/source-unclear funding for capital injection or settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions authorizing the transaction and payment routing; a detailed source-of-funds report tracing each remittance through original bank statements; signed intercompany financing or share-subscription agreements; short-form financial statements of the funding parent; and written legal confirmation that the transfer satisfies the Income Tax Act and related-party pricing rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity subscription or shareholder loan into the Canadian API wholesale corporation must be executed as SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the originating bank, with a Canadian correspondent receiving through Payments Canada Lynx for CAD or CHIPS/Fedwire for USD. For equity injection, Field 70 (Remittance Information) should identify the sender and use the ISO 20022/transaction purpose code, commonly 'A101 Capital investment - related enterprise' or 'EQUI Equity-related'; for shareholder loans, use 'A103 Financials loan - intercompany financing'. The receiving Canadian bank requires a board resolution approving the issuance of shares or the loan agreement, an updated National Register/registers, confirmation of Investment Canada Act filing status or exemption for a wholesale distribution acquisition, FINTRAC-compliant source-of-funds records, and any CBSA cross-border currency declaration if physical cash exceeds CAD 10,000; funds are then allocated to the Capital Escrow Account pending use and released to the Operational Account only after verification of the stated commercial purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct customer credits, SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank cover, and commercial documentary letters of credit issued as SWIFT MT700 under ICC UCP600 rules for import/export settlement of pharmaceutical APIs. CAD leg settles via Payments Canada Lynx (real-time large-value) or ACSS; USD leg clears through each Canadian bank's New York correspondent on CHIPS/Fedwire; documentary collections under URC522 via SWIFT MT797 serve as a secondary less-costly rail for low-risk repeat counterparties. Each outbound instruction must carry the correct purpose code, invoice and LC reference, product description consistent with the DEL, and must pass sanctions/pep screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) covering CAD/USD principal and interest
Vanilla EUR/USD and USD/CAD options (call/put with physical settlement)
Commercial forward with flexible settlement window (periodic option)

NDF (non-deliverable forward) is legally permissible where a non-resident counterparty requires USD/EUR or CAD referencing, but the Canadian market is fully deliverable, so NDF pricing against CAD is non-standard and carries valuation basis risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD $25 late filing fee; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution under CBCA subsection 212(2)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of default to 12 months; repeated non-filing may lead to criminal prosecution and forced dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Distributing corporations (public) must appoint an independent auditor under CBCA s.161. Non-distributing private corporations may waive the audit by unanimous shareholder resolution; an audit may nevertheless be required by the Director under CBCA, by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares, or by a court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Canadian GAAP for private enterprises) for private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA requires maintenance of a register of individuals with significant control (ISC register). The register must be updated annually and within 15 days of any change. No separate annual filing is required, but the annual return must be certified by a director as accurate; the ISC register is available for inspection by tax and enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate rate (Part I of the Income Tax Act); combined federal-provincial general rate ranges from 20% to 32% depending on the province/territory of permanent establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction reducing the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (subject to the CCPC definition — may be inapplicable to a foreign-controlled or listed corporation); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable/non-refundable investment tax credits (35%/15%); 100% immediate expensing of eligible manufacturing/processing assets; Flow-through share deductions for resource activities are not applicable to pharmaceutical wholesale; eligible Ontario (R&D) and Quebec tax credits may apply depending on permanent establishments
